replies.author: DeletedUser1209
replies.text:
I created an account just to respond to this. I'd the same problem for months. I stumbled upon a solution (that worked for me) purely by chance.

Sign into WhatsApp on a non-GOS device. I was on an old iPhone SE for about 3 months. In WhatsApp settings: add a passkey, turn on 2 step verification, add a password.

Now, what triggered a re-verification of my account was that I randomly changed my email address on WhatsApp from a generic simplelogin alias to a custom domain email. When I tried signing into WhatsApp on my GOS device after this, it worked!

Setup environment:

Owner profile

sandboxed play services - network, notifications, SMS permissions

Latest WhatsApp installed - network, notifications, SMS, mic (while using app) and contacts permissions

Although I've mentioned SMS permissions here, I was able to sign into my account with the passkey. My SIM wasn't even in the phone.

Please try this, and let me know if it works. I'd be very happy if it does.

replies.author: starglider
replies.text:
It seems like in most cases something happened to cause the user's risk score to increase. Using unofficial apps--ever--seems like a big one. They've probably just got a risk score per account, and once you pass a certain threshold, it mandates using the play integrity API.

One workaround is to install WA on an iPhone or play-certified android system and then use the web client on your GOS phone. You need to be sure the other app runs at least every 14 days, I think.
